memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But the people said to Joshua, "No! We will serve the Lord." Then Joshua said, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen to serve the Lord." "Yes, we are witnesses," they replied. "Now then," said Joshua, "throw away the foreign gods that are among you and yield your hearts to the Lord, the God of Israel." And the people said to Joshua, "We will serve the Lord our God and obey him." — Josh 24:21-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The people insist: "No! We will serve the Lord." Joshua then presses the commitment home. "You are witnesses against yourselves." He wants their decision to be conscious, deliberate, and owned. And he adds a searching command: "throw away the foreign gods that are among you and yield your hearts to the Lord."

Notice that even here, among people who had just pledged to serve God, there were still foreign gods hidden away. Their words said one thing, but their possessions told another story. Joshua calls them to make the outward and inward match — to get rid of the idols and to truly "yield your hearts."

This exposes something we all know too well. We can profess devotion to God while still holding on to secret idols. We say "I will serve the Lord," yet quietly cling to things that rival Him for our hearts. Real commitment means both throwing away the idols and yielding the heart — not one without the other.

God is not satisfied with words alone; He wants our hearts fully His. The Lord looks not merely at outward profession but at the heart (1 Sam 16:7). What foreign gods might still be tucked away in your life, even as you call yourself His? Bring them out, throw them away, and yield your heart wholly to the Lord who gave His Son for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there hidden "idols" you cling to while professing to serve God?
2. What does it mean for you to fully "yield your heart" to the Lord?
3. Does your outward profession match your inward devotion?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do not want a divided heart. Show me any idols I am hiding, help me throw them away, and take my heart fully as Your own. Amen.
